text:
Tampa Bay arrives on a high, 3-1-1 in its last five after a 6-4 win over Winnipeg, a Jets team now winless in seven. The Lightning are without Erik Cernak and Zemgus Girgensons, and the loudest story is off the ice: Daily Faceoff posted that Nikita Kucherov was lined up for the opening faceoff beside Steven Stamkos "one day after making his trade request public." Nashville is 1-2-2 in its last five and coming off a 4-3 home loss to Washington, with Stamkos facing his former team on game four of a five-game home stand.

The numbers favor Tampa Bay. At five on five, the Lightning have taken 56% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to Nashville's 45%, and our model projects 3.49 goals for TBL to 2.79 for NSH. The power play is a small edge too, 0.79 expected goals per game against 0.66, though Nashville's penalty kill is close to Tampa's.

In net, projected starter Andrei Vasilevskiy is at -2.7 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he's stopped relative to the quality of shots he's faced), but he was +23.2 over 58 games last year. Nashville's projected Justus Annunen, starting over Juuse Saros, is at -1.1 this year and +7.1 last year.

For Tampa Bay, Brandon Hagel has a 45% chance to score and Kucherov a 79% chance at a point. For Nashville, Stamkos and Filip Forsberg each sit at 34% to score, and Forsberg has goals in three straight, four in all.
